title: FILE STATUS 22 — VSAM duplicate-key on WRITE; legacy idiom branches to UPDATE-instead path
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. INSERT-OR-UPDATE.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-STAT  PIC X(2).
       01  WS-REC.
           05  WS-KEY  PIC X(10).
           05  WS-VAL  PIC 9(7)V99 COMP-3.
      *> WRITE on a KEYED VSAM file with a duplicate key returns
      *> FILE STATUS '22'. The legacy 'insert-or-update' idiom:
      *>   WRITE; IF STAT = '22' THEN REWRITE.
      *> Java/JDBC's MERGE or UPSERT is the natural target -- but the
      *> spec must surface the dup-key handling explicitly.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           WRITE WS-REC.
           IF WS-STAT = "22" REWRITE WS-REC.
           STOP RUN.
notes: Status 22 dup-key handling is the COBOL upsert idiom. A Java rewrite to MERGE / UPSERT (or ConcurrentHashMap.compute) is natural; the spec must capture the two-step semantic so the rewrite doesn't drop a step.
